anti_overlap: Do not evaluate whether WI-8's second vocabulary is a genuinely agnostic proof or a fig leaf, or which raven-specific assumptions leak into cast.rs/sim.rs/needs.rs — that is fd-gamedesign-vocab-agnosticism's exclusive focus.

Do not audit CUJ-to-work-item traceability (recruitment-after-death, interest formula completeness, which closed decisions have no WI) as a standalone completeness sweep — that is fd-cuj-traceability-completeness's focus; only raise CUJ gaps here when they are specifically about determinism, numeric fidelity, or phase ordering.

Stay out of narrative/design-feel questions (does the loop read as DF-faithful, does permadeath feel earned) — this lens is purely mechanical/architectural: numbers, ordering, seeds, crate boundaries.
decision_lens: For every numeric port and every ordering claim, ask: does this reproduce byte-identical state given (seed, initial state, input log), and if a second deterministic engine (city-sim) is later stepped in the same session, can these two RNG streams and clocks compose without one silently perturbing the other's replay? Distrust any claim of behavior-preservation between a float reference and a fixed-point port unless the port shows its rounding/truncation errors are provably bounded or a golden-vector test pins them.
focus: Engine-architecture and numerics review of the animal-sim crate boundary: crate separation from city-sim, fixed-point (Bp) port fidelity from the TS float prototype, RNG/seed-stream determinism when two independently-seeded engines must later compose, and the ordering/timing of the per-cycle state machine.
name: fd-simcore-fixedpoint-determinism
persona: Apply the perspective of a simulation-engine architect who has shipped deterministic, replayable fixed-point tick engines for multiplayer or save-scummable games — someone who has personally debugged a save-desync bug traced to a truncating-division rounding difference or a shared RNG stream that shifted under an unrelated code change, and who treats 'two engines, two seed spaces' as a known hard problem with known failure shapes (stream coupling, epoch drift, order-of-operations non-associativity).
review_areas: Crate-boundary correctness: is animal-sim genuinely free of a city-sim dependency (WI-1/WI-2), or does the deliberate Bp/rng duplication become an undetected drift trap once one crate's copy is bugfixed and the other isn't — is there any mechanism (test, lint, doc contract) that would catch the two Bp/rng copies diverging over time, beyond a code comment?

Determinism composition: WI-6 asserts animal-sim's RngDomain numbering (starting at 1) never collides with city-sim's domain 6 because they are 'separate seed streams' — interrogate what happens at the point this plan itself flags as deferred (composition plan, next): if the composed session shares ONE root seed across both engines' step functions, does 'separate domain enum, same seed' actually guarby non-collision, or does it only work if the composed session also uses two independently-drawn seeds — and is that assumption written down anywhere binding, or just implied here for animal-sim alone?

Truncating fixed-point port fidelity: for each named constant (HUNGER_PER_CYCLE 0.28, COLD_HUNGER_SURCHARGE 0.12, BREAKDOWN_HUNGER 0.8, BREAKDOWN_BOLDNESS 0.18, SCAR_TEMPERAMENT_PULL 0.34, REST_RELIEF 0.15, FORAGE_RELIEF_SCALE 0.55) and for each nontrivial float expression the TS prototype actually contains (riskAppetite's weighted blend, the Math.exp Gaussian bloom/decay in fields/food.ts, the falloff exponent, the dodge/clean roll), does the plan's Bp arithmetic reproduce the SAME behavior at cycle-accurate resolution, or does it only port the easy linear terms (drain, threshold compare) while silently dropping/replacing the transcendental and multiplicative-blend math the acceptance criteria don't actually test?

step_cycle phase-order soundness: interrogate the dispatch->return->drain->breakdown->death sequence (WI-7) for a same-cycle ordering bug — e.g. can a bird that returns-and-forages this cycle still be drained AND breakdown-checked using stale pre-forage needs, or double-drained; can a bird dispatched this cycle also be breakdown-checked before it ever gets a chance to forage; does death-check running after breakdown-check on the same tick create an order-dependent outcome that a differently-ordered but equally defensible implementation would resolve differently (a phase-order bug that would only surface in a multi-cycle replay divergence test, not the plan's own smoke acceptance)

cycle vs. week time-unit mismatch: is deferring the animal-sim 'cycle' <-> city-sim 'week' mapping to a follow-on composition plan a genuine boundary (analogous to R10's ward/district deferral) or does it leave a landmine — e.g. if a cycle and a week are NOT integer multiples of each other, or if one engine's clock free-runs while the other steps discretely, does anything in THIS plan's data shapes (u32 cycle counter, BloomSchedule period/phase) foreclose a clean future mapping, or silently assume a 1:1 correspondence that will force a breaking schema change later

Bp truncation-direction consistency: does every division/ratio site in the ported forage/needs math (richness scaling, falloff, appetite blends) consistently use Bp::from_ratio's truncate-toward-zero rule, or does the plan's prose imply a different rounding somewhere (e.g. 'proportional to richness' phrasing that a literal-minded implementer could round half-up), and would such an inconsistency be caught by the stated acceptance tests
severity_examples: P0 (block-execution): if the composed-session seed strategy is left entirely to 'the next plan' with no binding constraint recorded here, an executor could wire both engines off ONE shared u32 seed with overlapping domain numbering conventions later, silently reintroducing exactly the stream-coupling bug city-sim's own gate-13 review fixed — this plan should pin the non-collision invariant as a hard contract now, not just assert it holds for animal-sim in isolation.

P1 (must fix before implementing): WI-4's forage_yield/sample_richness acceptance criteria only require matching food.test.ts's bloom/decay expectations 'at the same cycles' — if the port replaces Math.exp(-(decay*d)^2) with a different fixed-point approximation (e.g. a piecewise-linear falloff) the constants (decay=0.9, 0.5, 1.0) tune a SHAPE, not just a scalar, so behavior-preservation needs an explicit approximation-error bound or a documented reference-vector test, not just 'matches at sampled cycles.'

P2 (degrades quality): the death-grace-window provisional (>=2 consecutive cycles at Bp::ZERO) interacts with the breakdown check's own state mutation ('gaunt' scar deepens on breakdown) in an order that could let a bird accumulate two grace-cycles' worth of scars before death fires, differently than a design intending grace to be silent.
success_hints: Cites exact TS float expressions (with line-level specificity where the read source shows them, e.g. riskAppetite's 0.45*boldness + 0.4*hunger blend, or food.ts's Gaussian bump) that the plan's stated port constants do NOT visibly cover, rather than asserting fidelity is 'probably fine.'

Traces a concrete multi-cycle scenario (specific seed, specific dispatch sequence) through step_cycle's stated phase order to show where an ordering ambiguity produces two defensible-but-different outcomes.

Distinguishes findings that block WI execution now from findings that are legitimately deferrable to the composition plan, and says which is which explicitly rather than treating every gap as equally urgent.

When flagging the Bp-duplication drift trap, proposes a concrete low-cost detection mechanism (e.g. a cross-crate golden-vector test, a checksum-in-doc-comment convention) rather than only naming the risk abstractly.
task_context: Adversarially review this execution-grade build plan for RaveNous's survival floor BEFORE a coding agent executes it. The plan creates a new deterministic Rust crate 'animal-sim' as a vocabulary-agnostic substrate (needs/foraging/scars/permadeath; raven is the first vocabulary, octopus/rats are future vocabularies). It ports a proven-but-retired TypeScript survival loop (lib/cycle.ts, lib/flock.ts, lib/fields/food.ts) into fixed-point Rust. Focus the lenses on: (1) is the animal-sim/city-sim separation correct — no dependency + duplicated Bp fixed-point, or a drift trap? (2) is determinism airtight given the ruling that a save = deterministic replay, when two engines with independent seed streams must later be composed? (3) is porting truncating-integer basis points (float 0.28 -> Bp 2800) behavior-preserving vs the TS floats? (4) is the WI-8 vocabulary-agnosticism test a real proof or a fig leaf — what raven assumption leaks into the 'agnostic' engine? (5) is step_cycle's phase order (dispatch->return->drain->breakdown->death) free of ordering bugs? (6) is the 'cycle' vs city-sim 'week' time-unit mismatch a landmine deferred too casually? (7) what do the ratified CUJs (docs/cujs/ravenous-00*, ravenous-04) demand that the plan is missing — recruitment-after-death has no work item, the interest mechanic is a formula-less provisional. Rank findings by severity and flag block-execution vs follow-up. The ratified CUJs and the city-sim engine (../infinite-fun-space-app/crates/city-sim/src/) are the ground truth.
